arxiv-2211-02601.title: Gravitational Analysis of Einstein-Non-Linear-Maxwell-Yukawa Black Hole under the Effect of Newman-Janis Algorithm
arxiv-2211-02601.creator: Rimsha Babar, Muhammad Asgher, Riasat Ali
arxiv-2211-02601.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rimsha Babar, Muhammad Asgher, Riasat Ali. In this paper, we analyze the rotating Einstein-non-linear-Maxwell-Yukawa black hole solution by Janis-Newman algorithmic rule and complex calculations. We investigate the basic properties (i.e., Hawking radiation) for the corresponding black hole solution. From the horizon structure of the black hole, we discuss the graphical behavior of Hawking temperature T H T_{H} and analyze the effects of spin parameter (appears due to Newman-Janis approach) on the T H T_{H} of black hole.

arxiv-2301-01365.title: James Webb Space Telescope: data, problems, and resolution Plenary talk at 36th Rencontres de Physique de la Vallée d’Aoste on Results and Perspectives in Particle Physics, extended and updated
arxiv-2301-01365.creator: A. D. Dolgov
arxiv-2301-01365.description: Abstract It is argued that the data presented by Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope, that seem to be at odds with the canonical big bang cosmology, find simple explanation if galaxy formation is seeded by massive primordial black holes (PBH), as anticipated in 1993 (A. Dolgov and J. Silk, later DS).

arxiv-2303-09983.title: Mitigating quantum decoherence in force sensors by internal squeezing
arxiv-2303-09983.creator: M. Korobko, J. Südbeck, S. Steinlechner, R. Schnabel
arxiv-2303-09983.description: Abstract The most efficient approach to laser interferometric force sensing to date uses monochromatic carrier light with its signal sideband spectrum in a squeezed vacuum state. Quantum decoherence, i.e. mixing with an ordinary vacuum state due to optical losses, is the main sensitivity limit.

arxiv-2308-04477.title: A Comparative Study of Code Generation using ChatGPT 3.5 across 10 Programming Languages
arxiv-2308-04477.creator: Alessio Buscemi
arxiv-2308-04477.description: Abstract Large Language Models are advanced Artificial Intelligence systems that have undergone extensive training using large datasets in order to understand and produce language that closely resembles that of humans. These models have reached a level of proficiency where they are capable of successfully completing university exams across several disciplines and generating functional code to handle novel problems.

arxiv-2410-14331.title: ChartifyText : Automated Chart Generation from Data-Involved Texts via LLM
arxiv-2410-14331.creator: Songheng Zhang, Lei Wang, Toby Jia-Jun Li, Qiaomu Shen, Yixin Cao and Yong Wang
arxiv-2410-14331.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Songheng Zhang, Lei Wang, Toby Jia-Jun Li, Qiaomu Shen, Yixin Cao and Yong Wang. Text documents with numerical values involved are widely used in various applications such as scientific research, economy, public health and journalism. However, it is difficult for readers to quickly interpret such data-involved texts and gain deep insights. To fill this research gap, this work aims to automatically generate charts to accurately convey the underlying data and ideas to readers, which is essentially a challenging task.

arxiv-2508-00325.title: PnP-DA: Towards Principled Plug-and-Play Integration of Variational Data Assimilation and Generative Models
arxiv-2508-00325.creator: Yongquan Qu, Matthieu Blanke, Sara Shamekh, Pierre Gentine
arxiv-2508-00325.description: Abstract Earth system modeling presents a fundamental challenge in scientific computing: capturing complex, multiscale nonlinear dynamics in computationally efficient models while minimizing forecast errors caused by necessary simplifications. Even the most powerful AI- or physics-based forecast system suffer from gradual error accumulation.

arxiv-2509-24645.title: Strong BSD for abelian surfaces and the Bloch-Beilinson conjecture
arxiv-2509-24645.creator: Kalyan Banerjee
arxiv-2509-24645.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove the Bloch-Beilinson conjecture for certain abelian surfaces over ℚ {\mathbb{Q}} , provided that the BSD is known for these abelian surfaces. 1. Introduction One of the most important problems in algebraic geometry is to compute the Chow groups for higher codimensional cycles on a smooth projective variety.

arxiv-2510-17858.title: Shortcutting Pre-trained Flow Matching Diffusion Models is Almost Free Lunch
arxiv-2510-17858.creator: Xu Cai, Yang Wu, Qianli Chen, Haoran Wu, Lichuan Xiang, Hongkai Wen
arxiv-2510-17858.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xu Cai, Yang Wu, Qianli Chen, Haoran Wu, Lichuan Xiang, Hongkai Wen. We present an ultra-efficient post-training method for shortcutting large-scale pre-trained flow matching diffusion models into efficient few-step samplers, enabled by novel velocity field self-distillation . While shortcutting in flow matching, originally introduced by shortcut models, offers flexible trajectory-skipping capabilities, it requires a specialized step-size embedding incompatible with existing models unless retraining from scratch—a process nearly as costly as pretraining itself.

arxiv-2511-19769.title: Blini: lightweight nucleotide sequence search and dereplication
arxiv-2511-19769.creator: Amit Lavon
arxiv-2511-19769.description: Abstract Blini is a tool for quick lookup of nucleotide sequences in databases, and for quick dereplication of sequence collections. It is meant to help clean and characterize large collections of assembled contigs or long sequences that would otherwise be too big to search with online tools, or too demanding for a local machine to process.

pmc-11548704.title: Surface Wetting Behaviors of Hydroxyl-Terminated Polybutadiene: Molecular Mechanism and Modulation
pmc-11548704.creator: Xinke Zhang, Zhikun Liu, Bing Yuan, Kai Yang, Fabrizio Olivito, Wan Abd Al Qadr Imad Wan-Mohtar, Goldie Harikrishna Oza
pmc-11548704.description: The surface wetting or coating of materials by polymers is crucial for designing functional interfaces and various industrial applications. However, the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. In this study, the wetting behavior of hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) on a quartz surface was systematically investigated using computer simulation methods.

pmc-11562072.title: Tuning Optical and Electrical Properties of Vanadium Oxide with Topochemical Reduction and Substitutional Tin
pmc-11562072.creator: Lance M. Wheeler, Thanh Luan Phan, Michelle A. Smeaton, Swagata Acharya, Shruti Hariyani, Marlena E. Alexander, Miranda I. Gonzalez, Elisa M. Miller, David W. Mulder, Sarbajit Banerjee, Katherine L. Jungjohann, Andrew J. Ferguson, Jeffrey L. Blackburn
pmc-11562072.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Vanadium oxides are widely tunable materials, with many thermodynamically stable phases suitable for applications spanning catalysis to neuromorphic computing. The stability of vanadium in a range of oxidation states enables mixed-valence polymorphs of kinetically accessible metastable materials. Low-temperature synthetic routes to, and the properties of, these metastable materials are poorly understood and may unlock new optoelectronic and magnetic functionalities for expanded applications.

pmc-12472169.title: Carbon-Induced Structural Evolution and Synergistic Enhancement of Wear and Corrosion Resistance in (AlFeCoNi)C High-Entropy Alloy Carbide Films
pmc-12472169.creator: Duoli Chen, Yefeng Zhou, Xianting Yang, Mengyuan Guo, Jun Liang, Deming Huang, Yu Ni, Yurong Zhou, Yantao Li, Xin Jiang
pmc-12472169.description: The (AlFeCoNi)C high-entropy alloy carbide films (HECFs) with tunable carbon contents were fabricated by magnetron sputtering to investigate the carbon-driven structural evolution and its coupling effects on mechanical and chemical properties. With increasing carbon incorporation (0–47.6 at.%), the HECFs formed a composite structure of amorphous phase and BCC nanocrystalline phase, as evidenced by XRD and TEM.

pmc-12523209.title: Effect of noise isolation with noise-cancelling earmuffs during laparoscopic surgery on acute postoperative pain: a clinical randomised controlled trial
pmc-12523209.creator: Teng Wu, Hongwei Qi, Kangli Hui, Ying Hu, Miaomiao Xu, Jiejie Zhou, Manlin Duan
pmc-12523209.description: BackgroundAcute postoperative pain is common in surgical patients, and intraoperative noise isolation has been shown to reduce pain for up to 24 h postoperatively. However, acute postoperative pain primarily occurs during the first three days after surgery, and it remains unclear whether intraoperative noise isolation affects the incidence of moderate-to-severe acute postoperative pain during this period.

pmc-12753239.title: Structural characterization of zebrafish Ngly2, an ovary-enriched acid PNGase required for egg-free glycan production
pmc-12753239.creator: Akinobu Honda, Katsuhiko Kamada, Junichi Seino, Hiroto Hirayama, Haruhiko Fujihira, Masashi Ueki, Toshiyuki Shiraki, Raymond N Burton-Smith, Kazuyoshi Murata, Nozomi Ishii, Ichiro Matsuo, Tadashi Suzuki
pmc-12753239.description: Peptide:N-glycanase (PNGase) is a deglycosylating enzyme acting on asparagine(N)-linked glycans on glycoproteins. It is well established that fish possesses two PNGases with distinct properties. One is a cytosolic PNGase (NGLY1 in humans), active at neutral pH and widely conserved among eukaryotes.

pmc-13241779.title: Seasonal dynamic and individual determinants of Amphibiocystidium sp. infection in the palmate newt during the aquatic breeding season
pmc-13241779.creator: Léa Lorrain-Soligon, François Brischoux
pmc-13241779.description: Amphibian populations are undergoing global declines, with infectious diseases playing a major role in these losses. While chytridiomycosis has been widely studied, other pathogens, such as mesomycetozoean parasites, are increasingly recognized as potential contributors to amphibian health deterioration. In this study, we investigated the seasonal dynamics of Amphibiocystidium sp.

pmc-13411840.title: From Host-Microbiome Symbiosis to Clinical Translation: A Gut Microbiome Perspective on Radiation Enteritis
pmc-13411840.creator: Jieru Zhuang, Yun Zhong, Zhongyao Lin, Yongjun Lu, Hui Wang, Lingming Chen, Keli Yang, Delin Tan, Yunyi Qiu, Yuanxin Zhang, Huaiming Wang, Zhenhuang Ge
pmc-13411840.description: Radiotherapy is an essential component of multimodal treatment for solid tumors, and more than half of patients with cancer receive radiation during their disease course. Because of the unique anatomical and physiological features of the intestine, radiation enteritis (RE) remains a common and clinically challenging complication of abdominal and pelvic irradiation, with limited effective treatment options.

pmc-13469487.title: Contextual Influences on Parenting and Adversity: An Examination of Multisystemic Effects
pmc-13469487.creator: Sierra N. Walters, Jacqueline B. Duong, Kayla E. Carta, Grace A. Jumonville, Alyssa S. Carrasco, Daniela N. Romero, Matthew W. Ahle, Theodora Chaspari, Shrikanth S. Narayanan, Jonathan S. Comer, Adela C. Timmons
pmc-13469487.description: The ability of a child to demonstrate resilience is a complex outcome influenced by multiple interconnected social systems. One system important to child resiliency is the family system, specifically parenting and the parent-child relationship. However, less is known about how macrosocial systems may affect the family system and, in turn, resiliency at the individual level.

pmc-13476524.creator: Jie Zhang, Binghe Xiao, Zhiliang Wang, Xiang Li

pmc-13677662.title: Effects of Culture History and Algal Taxonomy on Bacterial Communities in Long-maintained Filamentous Green Algae
pmc-13677662.creator: Ethan Wood, Bente Edvardsen, Kari Skjånes, Luka Šupraha
pmc-13677662.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Algal cultures are widely used to study algae–bacteria interactions, yet the relative roles of algal taxonomy, culturing environment, and historical contingency in shaping bacterial communities of long-maintained monoalgal cultures remain unclear. uslaw-usc-t12-s1978.title: 12 U.S.C. § 1978 — Actions under other Federal or State laws unaffected; regulations or orders barred as a defense
uslaw-usc-t12-s1978.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s1978.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 22 (Tying Arrangements). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Nothing contained in this chapter shall be construed as affecting in any manner the right of the United States or any other party to bring an action under any other law of the United States or of any State, including any right which may exist.

uslaw-usc-t28-s871.title: 28 U.S.C. § 871 — Clerk, chief deputy clerk, assistant clerk, deputies, assistants, and other employees
uslaw-usc-t28-s871.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s871.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part III (Court Officers And Employees); Chapter 55 (Court Of International Trade). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Court of International Trade may appoint a clerk, a chief deputy clerk, an assistant clerk, deputy clerks, and such deputies, assistants, and other employees as may be necessary for the effective dispatch of the business.
